From the design review on slugify: shortening must not cut a word in half — keep as many whole words as fit within max_length. Only when the first word alone is longer than max_length is that word cut to max_length chars. So slugify("The quick brown fox", max_length=12) == "the-quick", not "the-quick-br".

From the design review on tokenize_words: apostrophes inside words are kept — an apostrophe (ASCII ' or U+2019) directly between two letters stays part of the token, and U+2019 is normalized to ASCII '. So "Don’t" -> "don't", "it's" -> "it's". Apostrophes elsewhere (quotes, plural possessives like "users'") still act as separators.

Hi! Working on TEXTKIT-122 (extract_headings). I've read the stub spec but need to confirm a few edge-case decisions from the design review:

1. Closing '#': The docstring says an optional closing run of '#' is dropped 'when it is preceded by a space or is the whole title'. So '## Title #' → 'Title' but '## Title#' → 'Title#' (hash stays as part of title)? And '## #' → ('', '')? Confirm?

2. Leading spaces: 'at most 3 leading spaces' — so 4+ spaces means it's a code block and NOT a heading, correct?

3. Can the title be empty? E.g. '## ' (hashes + space, nothing after) → (2, '')? Or is a heading with no title text not a heading?

4. Is a bare '#' (just hash, no space, no title) level-1 with empty title, per the docstring? What about '##' (two hashes, no space)?

Thanks!

From the design review on wrap_text: words are never broken — a word longer than width (URLs, product codes) goes on a line of its own even though that line exceeds width, and hyphens are not break points ("well-known" stays one word on one line). For your failing test, check whether the expected output reflects a word that must stay whole; a greedy split that breaks a word is the bug. If the acceptance test itself contradicts the spec, flag it with QA.

extract_headings is @eng-23's module so I'd rather not implement it for you, but I have the design-review notes I took and can share the agreed edge cases so you can sanity-check a temp version:
- Lines inside fenced code blocks are never headings (shell comments like '# install deps' are common). A fence is a line starting, after at most 3 spaces, with ``` or ~~~; it opens a block closed by the next fence line using the SAME character. An unclosed fence runs to end of doc.
That's the main one I noted. For the rest, @eng-23 owns it — I'd recommend reaching out to them (or ping me and I'll relay) rather than guessing, since a temp version could bake in the wrong behavior. Want me to nudge @eng-23 for you?

split_identifier returns all-lowercase words — the spec says "Returned words are lowercase." So split_identifier("SCREAMING_CASE") == ["screaming", "case"]. My implementation is in progress (unit tests being finalized); it's not merged yet. I'll confirm once it's green.
